My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for generations. My father grew wheat and corn, his father grew wheat and corn, and I grow wheat and corn. The North China Plain is built for this rotation — the soil knows it, the buyers expect it, and I know how to do it well. I have 12 mu of land. I am not going to gamble on vegetables or cotton like some younger men tried. They had bad years, I did not.

For wheat, I planted last October with Kenong 199 seeds — the agricultural station recommended them and I have had good harvests. Now heading into spring I will do my jointing irrigation and topdress with urea. I apply nitrogen heavily because I cannot afford a thin harvest. My father always said feed the land and the land feeds you. I spray herbicide in the fall and hit it again with a fungicide before heading — powdery mildew has hurt neighbors who skipped it.

After wheat harvest in June I go straight into maize. No plowing — I seed Xianyu 335 directly into the stubble. Saves me three or four days of work and money on diesel. Compound fertilizer at planting, urea at trumpet stage. Summer rains handle most of the water but I keep one irrigation ready at silking if it goes dry.

I keep my plan simple and manageable for one man.
